entries.title: Psalms 78:1
segments: A historic psalm, for the instruction of God's covenant people.  It was probably written in David's day, and ends with his elevation to the throne.

entries.title: Psalms 78:2
segments: Parable--dark sayings; see note to

. 
 
Many of the instructions and truths of the Bible are dark sayings to those who reject them, while they are plain and highly useful to those who believe and obey them.

entries.title: Psalms 78:4
segments: A knowledge of the past dealings of God should be communicated by parents to their children, as a means of leading them to adore him, and preparing them to transmit the knowledge of his perfections to those who come after them.

entries.title: Psalms 78:5
segments: Make them known; the testimony and law just spoken of.

entries.title: Psalms 78:8
segments:
Set not their heart aright; did not heartily obey God. 
 
Men must keep their hearts with all diligence, if they would have their lives directed according to his precepts.

entries.title: Psalms 78:9
segments:
The children of Ephraim; here representing the whole people.  They seem to be specially named because they were the leading tribe before the time of the kings. 
 
  Turned back; the reference is not probably to any particular recorded event, but to their general unbelief and unfaithfulness.

entries.title: Psalms 78:12
segments: Zoan; one of the principal cities of Egypt.
No displays of the mercies or judgments of God will lead men to love and obey him; but whatever may be the manifestations of himself, without his grace they will continue to rebel against him.

entries.title: Psalms 78:13
segments: He divided the sea; at the time of the deliverance of Israel from Egypt.

entries.title: Psalms 78:18
segments: They tempted God; by distrusting his power, truth, and love.

entries.title: Psalms 78:21
segments: A fire was kindled; see

. 
 
Unbelief of divine testimony is a great sin, and God is angry with those who indulge it.  They treat him as if he were a liar, and cut themselves off from the blessings of his salvation.

entries.title: Psalms 78:24
segments: Corn of heaven; manna, which came from above.

entries.title: Psalms 78:25
segments: Angels' food; the manna is so called from its excellence as coming from heaven.

entries.title: Psalms 78:27
segments: Blessings greatly desired may be given in judgment, and be the occasion of ruin to those who receive them.

entries.title: Psalms 78:33
segments: Their days did he consume in vanity, and their years in trouble; the reference is to the wearisome sojourn of forty years in the wilderness, during which time all the men who came out of Egypt were wasted away.  Compare

. 
 
Continuance in sin causes continuance of trouble, and though great afflictions may produce external reformation, yet if the heart be not turned to God, the outward profession of love to him will be hypocrisy.

entries.title: Psalms 78:34
segments: Slew them; many of them; and visited others with sore calamities.

entries.title: Psalms 78:36
segments: They lied; by an insincere profession of love and obedience.

entries.title: Psalms 78:38
segments: God shows his compassion by waiting long even upon flagrant transgressors, and often by removing from them temporal calamities and continuing to bless them, notwithstanding their sins, in proof that he desires not their death, but that they should turn and live.

entries.title: Psalms 78:41
segments: Limited the Holy One; by ascribing bounds to his power.

entries.title: Psalms 78:43
segments: The field of Zion; the region about the city.

entries.title: Psalms 78:47
segments: With frost; rather, with hailstones.

entries.title: Psalms 78:51
segments: The tabernacles of Ham; the dwelling-places of the Egyptians, his descendants.

entries.title: Psalms 78:52
segments: God will make a way for his chosen people, and grant them deliverance; but his enemies, however numerous and powerful, will be destroyed.

entries.title: Psalms 78:54
segments:
The border of his sanctuary; the boundary of the holy land. 
 
  This mountain; Zion, as now the central point of the nation.  See

entries.title: Psalms 78:57
segments: Like a deceitful bow; not accomplishing the end for which they were made.

entries.title: Psalms 78:60
segments:
Shiloh; a place in the tribe of Ephraim in which had been kept the ark of God, the symbol of his presence. 
 
The withdrawal of God's presence from a people on account of their sins, is a forerunner of dreadful calamities, and often of approaching ruin.

entries.title: Psalms 78:61
segments: His strength--his glory; the ark, which was the emblem of these, and which was taken captive by the Philistines.

entries.title: Psalms 78:63
segments: Not given to marriage; literally, not praised, that is, in nuptial songs, according to the custom of the age.

entries.title: Psalms 78:64
segments: Their widows made no lamentation; the meaning seems to be, that the bodies of the slain were left to perish on the field of battle, so that their widows could not mourn over them, as was done at a regular funeral.  Compare
and especially

entries.title: Psalms 78:65
segments: The Lord awaked; arose for the deliverance of his people.

entries.title: Psalms 78:66
segments: God may permit the wicked to triumph for a time, as a punishment of his people; but their triumph will be short, and their punishment without end.

entries.title: Psalms 78:67
segments: Refused the tabernacle of Joseph; refused to have his descendants, the tribe of Ephraim, longer govern the people.

entries.title: Psalms 78:68
segments:
Chose the tribe of Judah; to have the preeminence, as furnishing the royal family. 
 
  The mount Zion; as the site of the tabernacle, and afterwards of the temple.  Moriah was reckoned as a part of Zion. 
 
Civil power is the gift of God.  He takes it from one and gives it to another, as seemeth good in his sight; and holds all who receive it accountable to him for its use.

entries.title: Psalms 78:69
segments: His sanctuary; the temple, or place of public worship.
